title: RFdiffusion3 Unifies All-Atom Biomolecular Diffusion for DNA Binders & Multi-Turnover Enzymes
whyItMatters: Unifies protein design at full atomic resolution—running ~10× faster than RFdiffusion2 to generate sequence-specific DNA binders and 35 experimentally validated multi-turnover cysteine hydrolases.
summary: Published in Science on October 15, 2026 by Jasper Butcher, Rohith Krishna, and David Baker’s team at the University of Washington Institute for Protein Design, RFdiffusion3 (RFD3) replaces coarse residue-frame representations with a unified all-atom diffusion architecture modeling up to 14 atoms per residue alongside arbitrary nucleic acids, small molecules, and metal cofactors. Running roughly 10× faster than RFdiffusion2 while generalizing across protein-DNA, protein-ligand, and catalytic active-site scaffolding, RFD3 designed sequence-specific DNA-binding proteins (EC50 = 5.89 μM) and 35 functional multi-turnover cysteine hydrolase enzymes reaching kcat/Km = 3,557 M⁻¹s⁻¹.
technicalHighlights: Models full all-atom biomolecular coordinates (backbone + side chains + DNA/small-molecule/cofactor atoms) in a single diffusion architecture, running ~10× faster than RFdiffusion2.
Experimentally generated de novo sequence-specific DNA-binding proteins and 35 distinct multi-turnover cysteine hydrolase enzymes (up to kcat/Km = 3,557 M⁻¹s⁻¹).
Released open-source via the Baker Lab RosettaCommons / Foundry ecosystem, making atomic-precision biomolecular design accessible across academic labs.
caveats: Still requires downstream sequence design (LigandMPNN / ProteinMPNN) and in-silico filtering before wet-lab synthesis; catalytic efficiencies of de novo enzymes remain below the fastest natural enzymes.
institutions: University of Washington (Institute for Protein Design)

scoreRationale.foundational: Completes the transition of generative protein diffusion from backbone-only scaffolds to unified all-atom biomolecular interaction design.
scoreRationale.ripple: Open-source all-atom generator applicable across gene regulation (DNA binders), small-molecule biosensing, and industrial biocatalysis.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Science (Oct 2026) with experimental biochemical validation of DNA binders and 35 active multi-turnover enzymes.
scoreRationale.velocity: Delivers ~10× generation speedup over RFdiffusion2 while solving complex multi-component atomic scaffolding tasks directly.
